name: Jadesserts
tagline: A little box of sweet surprises

shape.motif: heart bullets + pastel confetti (circles, sparkles, hearts); a 4-segment pastel bar that stands for the 4 items in the box

do: Warm cream is the default background; stage colours are pastels (pink, lavender, mint, peach)
Use heart glyphs as the list bullet and confetti shapes for texture
Everything rounded; soft, bouncy motion (overshoot) rather than mechanical
Price is its own oversized callout
dont: No stark white or grey backgrounds, no black shadows (tint shadows plum/pink)
Never put white small text on the coral primary (3.1:1) — display sizes only
No more than one saturated coral block per scene

_notes.fonts: Baloo 2 + Quicksand are the design system's flagged substitutes for the real bubble wordmark font. If they cannot load (offline/proxy), the fallback stack renders instead; supply woff2/ttf via type.fontFiles to render exactly.
_notes.extraRoles: blush, blushDeep, primaryDeep, mint, lavender, white are Jadesserts-specific extras used for the sweet box, outlines and hearts.
_notes.toyRoles: toyYellow, bone, wood, cardboard, glass are toy-world roles used by kits/brickworld.mjs (brick-people skin, skeleton, props, signs, windows).

_identityStatus: DRAFT identity sections (strategy, voiceGuide, logoRules, imagery, sound, contact, paletteNames) written by Claude from the brand’s existing look and copy. Confirm or edit with the owner.

strategy.mission: Make every sweet moment feel like a gift: small-batch treats, packed with care into a box worth opening.
strategy.vision: The first name people think of when they want to surprise someone with something sweet.
strategy.promise: A little box of sweet surprises, worth every wait.
strategy.positioning: For people who show love with food, Jadesserts is the home bakery whose curated sweet boxes turn an ordinary day into an occasion.
values: Made with love, made in small batches

audience.name: The gifter
audience.need: a thoughtful, pretty present that arrives ready to wow

audience.name: The treat-yourselfer
audience.need: a weekly reward that feels special

audience.name: The party planner
audience.need: boxes for birthdays, office treats and events

personality.archetype: The Caregiver with a playful streak

pillars.name: Sweet, not sugary
pillars.means: Warm and affectionate, with a wink.
pillars.notMeans: Baby talk or endless exclamation marks.

pillars.name: Playful
pillars.means: Small jokes, food puns, reality-TV drama about dessert.

pillars.name: Generous
pillars.means: Lead with what’s inside the box and why it’s a treat.

examples.good: Your sweet box is ready. Go on, treat someone.

examples.bad: Our products are of high quality.
examples.good: Baked this morning. Boxed with love.

misuse: Never separate the cherries from the wordmark in the main lock-up
Never set the logo on coral without a cream panel behind it

imagery.style: Bright, soft, high-key food photography on cream or pastel backgrounds; treats cut out cleanly and shown whole, never cropped mid-bite. Illustrations are rounded, pastel and toy-like.
do: Shoot from slightly above with soft daylight
Show the box open with the treats arranged
Use pastel props: ribbons, hearts, confetti

iconography.style: Filled, rounded shapes: hearts, cherries, sparkles, scalloped badges. No thin-line icons.

sound.music: Music-box plucks, bells and soft bass at ~120 bpm.
sound.sonicLogo: A rising four-note chime on the logo reveal.
sound.voice: Warm, smiling female narrator; character voices for comedy spots; captions on every line.
